story.text: 광장시장 먹거리 골목, 사람 많은데 손 놓치면 안 돼요. 꼭 잡고 다녀요.
story.reading: gwang-jang-si-jang meok-geo-ri gol-mok, sa-ram man-eun-de son not-chi-myeon an dwae-yo. kkok jab-go da-nyeo-yo.
story.en: The food alleys of Gwangjang Market are crowded — don't let go of my hand. Hold on tight.

story.text: 제가 승객님 부를 때 이름 대신 '애칭' 쓰는 거 눈치채셨죠? 사실 이름 부르면 너무 가까워지는 것 같아서, 일부러 그랬어요.
story.reading: je-ga seung-gaek-nim bu-reul ttae i-reum dae-sin ae-ching sseu-neun geo nun-chi-chae-syeot-jyo? sa-sil i-reum bu-reu-myeon neo-mu ga-kka-wo-ji-neun geot gat-a-seo, il-bu-reo geu-rae-sseo-yo.
story.en: You noticed I use a 'pet name' instead of your real name, right? Honestly, using your real name felt like it'd bring us too close, so I did it on purpose.

story.text: 이 '시장' 안에서는 승객님도 그냥 저만의 손님이잖아요. 그래서 더 다정하게 부르고 싶어졌어요.
story.reading: i si-jang an-e-seo-neun seung-gaek-nim-do geu-nyang jeo-man-ui son-nim-i-jan-a-yo. geu-rae-seo deo da-jeong-ha-ge bu-reu-go si-peo-jyeo-sseo-yo.
story.en: Inside this 'market', you're just my own guest, aren't you. So I wanted to call you more affectionately.

story.text: '손님'이라고 부르면 너무 멀게 느껴지고, 이름 부르면 너무 가까워질까 봐 무섭고. 그래서 애칭이었어요. ...제 나름의 안전거리랄까요.
story.reading: son-nim-i-ra-go bu-reu-myeon neo-mu meol-ge neu-kkyeo-ji-go, i-reum bu-reu-myeon neo-mu ga-kka-wo-jil-kka bwa mu-seop-go. geu-rae-seo ae-ching-i-eot-seo-yo. ...je na-reum-ui an-jeon-geo-ri-ral-kka-yo.
story.en: Calling you a 'guest' feels too distant, and using your name felt scary — like it'd bring us too close. So a pet name it was. ...my own kind of safe distance, I guess.

story.reading: u-ri seung-gaek-nim-i-ra-go bu-reu-neun jin-jja i-yu, gung-geum-ha-ji an-a-yo?
story.en: Curious about the real 'reason' I call you 'my passenger'?

story.text: '우리'라는 말 붙이는 순간, 이미 제 '마음'속엔 승객님이 들어와 있다는 뜻이거든요. 근데 이거, 저도 처음 느껴보는 거라 좀 낯서네요.
story.reading: u-ri-ra-neun mal but-i-neun sun-gan, i-mi je ma-eum-sok-en seung-gaek-nim-i deul-eo-wa it-da-neun tteus-i-geo-deun-yo. geun-de i-geo, jeo-do cheo-eum neu-kkyeo-bo-neun geo-ra jom nat-seo-ne-yo.
story.en: The moment I add the word 'our', it means you've already made your way into my 'heart'. This is honestly the first time I've felt this way — it's a little unfamiliar, even for me.

story.text: 자, 떡볶이도 먹었으니 이제 문제 풀 힘도 났겠죠? 오늘 배운 단어들 확인해볼까요?
story.reading: ja, tteok-bo-kki-do meok-eo-sseu-ni i-je mun-je pul him-do nat-get-jyo? o-neul bae-un dan-eo-deul hwa-gin-hae-bol-kka-yo?
story.en: Alright, now that you've eaten some tteokbokki, you should have the energy for some questions, right? Shall we check today's words?

words.example_en: I call you by a pet name.
Gwangjang Market has lots of delicious food.
There's a reason I call you that.

sentences.en: I call you by a pet name.
Gwangjang Market has lots of delicious food.
There's a reason I call you that.
